---
title: "pivot_wider() does not accept the positional arguments of spread()"
ref: TDY-11
categories: [tidyverse]
impact: cryptique
attendu: "the same wide table as with `spread(long, key, val)`"
versions: "All versions of {tidyr} since 1.0.0"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2019)"
---

::: {.piege packages="tidyr"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tidyr))

long <- data.frame(id = c(1, 1, 2, 2), key = c("a", "b", "a", "b"), val = 1:4)
spread(long, key, val)
pivot_wider(long, key, val)
```
:::

## Why

`spread()` took the names column and the values column in second and third position. `pivot_wider()`, its replacement, put `...` right after the data: every other argument must be named. So `key` and `val` fall into `...`, and `names_from` keeps its default value, a column called `name`.

The error talks about a `name` column you never wrote, which does not put you on the right track.

## The remedy

Name `names_from` and `values_from`.

::: {.piege packages="tidyr"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tidyr))

pivot_wider(long, names_from = key, values_from = val)
```
:::
